_comment: SALVAGE kit: a hand-run weld seam - a bead down the straight edge of a hull with four lumps of DIFFERENT size on it, wandering either side of the line, and a doubler plate over one end. Deliberately NOT the `ribs` primitive: even ribbing reads as a machined surface, and the point here is a bead a person laid badly. Long axis Z and 0.92 of a cell long, so `align: Run` runs it down the edge and consecutive plates join into ONE unbroken bead rather than a dotted row. Its rule then stops the bead one cell short of each end of the run, so a seam ends mid-edge - a repair that ran out where the salvaged plate did, which is a story, where a dotted row is only noise.
